chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Therefore bear up patiently as did the Determined Ones from the Messengers bear up with'.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Nuh, and Ibrahim, and Musa, and Isa, and Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)'.

I said, 'How did they come to be the Determined Ones?' He said: 'Because Nuh was sent with a Book and a Law, and everyone who came after Nuh took by the Book of Nuh, and his Law and his manifesto, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came with the Parchments, and with determination he neglected the Book of Nuh, not having disbelieved in it.'

So every Prophet who came after Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took by the Law of Ibrahim, and his manifesto, and by the Parchments, until Musa came with the Torah and his Law, and his manifesto, and with determination he neglected the Parchments.

And every Prophet who came after Musa (peace be upon him) took by the Torah, and his Law, and his manifesto, until the Messiah (peace be upon him) came with the Evangel, and with determination he neglected the Law of Musa, as well as his manifesto.
So every Prophet who came after the Messiah adhered to his Law and his manifesto, until Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) came. So he came with the Quran and with his Law and his manifesto.
Thus, his Permissible is a Permissible up to the Day of Judgement, and his Prohibition is a Prohibition up to the Day of Judgement.
So, these are the Determined Ones from the Messengers (peace be upon them).

key_terms.أُولُو الْعَزْمِ: The Determined Ones (a specific title for five major prophets)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five Ulul-Azm prophets and how is their status defined in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the theological concept of 'Ulul-Azm' by linking it to the progressive abrogation (naskh) of previous divine laws, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes a hierarchical lineage where each major Prophet superseded the preceding one's specific legislation, culminating in Muhammad (peace be upon him) whose Quranic rulings are final and eternal. This narrative underscores the continuity of prophethood while affirming the supremacy and permanence of the final revelation.

en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ’Isa from Sama’a ibn Mahran who has reported the following: “Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Exercise patience as the messengers who possessed determination had exercised patience. . . . ’[46:35]
The Imam said, ‘They were Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad, recipient of divine supreme covenant.’
I then asked, ‘How did they become messengers who possessed great determination?’

The Imam replied, ‘It was because Noah had received a book from Allah and a system of laws and those who came after Noah, they followed his book and his system of laws until Abraham came with books and firm determination. He left the book of Noah aside but not out of rejection.

Thereafter every prophet followed the system of laws of Abraham and his books (al-Suhuf) until Moses came with the Torah, his system of laws and with firm determination. He left the books (al-Suhuf) aside.
Every prophet thereafter followed the Torah and the system of laws of Moses until Jesus came with the Gospel and firm determination. He left aside the system of laws of Moses.
Every prophet thereafter followed the system of laws of Jesus until Prophet Muhammad (a.s.) came. He brought the Holy Quran and his system of laws (the Shari’a).
All that is lawful in his system of laws will remain lawful until the Day of Judgment and all that is unlawful in his system of laws will remain unlawful until the Day of Judgment.
This is how the messengers who possessed firm determination have been.’”
